FOURTH PRIMARY = YES. The others are Fedward (2307.00356), BRFL (2310.13403) and DROP (2502.07011). This row matters most for what it does to the shape of the finding: DROP established that a missing identifying contrast is not a symptom of weak work, and DP2Guard establishes that it is not a symptom of a narrow evaluation either. This paper runs 300 rounds on three datasets against four poisoning attacks at five malicious-client ratios under two partitions, adds a deep-leakage reconstruction study for the privacy claim, a per-iteration and per-client overhead study, an asymptotic complexity table against four cryptographic baselines, and a formal simulator-based privacy proof. It then takes its own composition apart exactly once, at the one knob that cannot identify anything.

THE C-d = NO IS THE SAFESPARSE COUNTERFACTUAL, REALIZED. SafeSparse's row records that had that paper swept only γ -- the downstream stage's own sensitivity -- rather than also β -- the upstream filter's threshold -- it would have coded C-d = NO and become a primary. DP2Guard is that case: its only sweep is the terminal trust stage's own smoothing constant. The direction is wrong in the same way DROPlet's was, and for a different structural reason: DROPlet deleted the downstream stage, while DP2Guard re-parameterizes it. Both leave the audit's question unanswered, because neither ever asks how a fixed mechanism behaves as a function of what reaches it.

I ALSO CHECKED THE READING THAT WOULD DESTROY THE PRIMARY, AND IT PROVES TOO MUCH. One could argue that the trust score is upstream of the weighted aggregation, so sweeping β varies an upstream stage while a downstream mechanism -- the weighted sum -- is held fixed, which would make C-d = YES under rule 4. I rejected it because every defense terminates in an aggregation step, so admitting a weighted sum as the "downstream mechanism" would make C-d true of any paper that sweeps any parameter at all, and the criterion would be vacuous. The frozen text asks for the downstream MECHANISM to be held fixed while the upstream stage varies; a weighted mean whose weights are the thing being varied is not a mechanism held fixed, it is the arithmetic of the variation. This is the sharpest statement of where I draw that line, and A5 should state it explicitly, because four of the frame's C-d = YES codes come through the hyperparameter route and a reader has to know which sweeps count.

C-b IS THE SAME PAIRING REASON AS DROP'S, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING AS A CONVERGENCE. Both papers compose a per-round geometric detector with a cross-round behavioural memory, and both justify the second by a failure mode of the first that is stated in attack terms -- DROP names the per-round majority assumption, DP2Guard names the on-off adversary. Two papers reaching the identical composition rationale from unrelated literatures (backdoor defense with distillation; privacy-preserving IIoT FL with blockchain) is evidence that the outcome-gated DESIGN is a recurring pattern rather than an artifact of one community, and A4 can use the pair for that.

BOTH C-c AND C-d BUCKETS UNDERPERFORMED. C-c returned zero candidates for the eighth time, on the same accuracy-only signature. C-d returned three candidates, all of them attack definitions or simulator constructions, and missed the β study; the β study surfaced from a caption enumeration, which is now the reliable method for this failure mode. Ninth C-d miss. Crucially, the miss here would have been HARMLESS to the primary -- the aid's failure and the correct code point the same way -- but the caption enumeration is what makes the C-d = NO defensible rather than merely unrefuted, and A5 should describe it as the standard negative-search procedure for every primary row.
